samples.summary: Editor usernames + edit timestamps are now persisted at rest in the note CRDT, where unauthenticated view-only share-link visitors can read them
samples.evidence: Before this change `root.content` held only markdown; editor identity existed solely in ephemeral Yorkie presence, visible only to clients co-present at that moment. `editText` now stamps `{ a: <username>, t: Date.now() }` onto every inserted run (yorkie-note-store.ts:91-94), where `a` is `currentUser.username` (notes-detail.tsx:259) or the share-link visitor's username (shared-document.tsx:890). Those attributes are part of the CRDT and are replicated to every client that attaches to `note-<id>`. The Yorkie auth webhook grants read to any share-link holder regardless of role — `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200` returns `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true` — so an unauthenticated visitor holding a *view-only* link can attach and read the full authorship history: every workspace member's username who ever edited the note plus per-edit epoch-ms timestamps (an activity-timing side channel), including people who are not and never were online during that visit. Attacker action: open a viewer share link, read `doc.getRoot().content.values()` (or the bundled Yorkie devtools) in the console. The backend REST/CLI path is unaffected (`readNoteRoot` returns `text.toString()` only, note-content.ts:46), so the exposure is entirely on the Yorkie replication channel and is not mediated by the UI toggle. Nothing in the design doc addresses share-link readers; it only disclaims audit-trail status.

samples.summary: Blame attribution is derived entirely from client-controlled presence with no server-side verification, so any editor can forge another user's authorship
samples.evidence: `localAuthorName()` reads `this.doc.getMyPresence()?.name` (yorkie-note-store.ts:135) — a value the client itself set at attach time (notes-detail.tsx:259, shared-document.tsx:890). Presence content is never validated: I found no server-side check of presence or of `Text` attributes (yorkie-auth.controller.ts only authorizes doc key + verb; yorkie-event.controller.ts has no username/identity handling; note-content.ts ignores attributes). A malicious client with write access — including an *anonymous* share-link visitor, since yorkie-auth.controller.ts:200 grants `rw` to `link.role === 'editor'` with no login — can call `presence.set({ name: 'victim-username' })`, or write the attributes directly as `content.edit(from, to, text, { a: 'victim-username', t: Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER })`. Because `authorOfRange` picks the run with the largest `at` (blame-gutter.ts:48) and `t` is a client-supplied `Date.now()`, a forged far-future timestamp lets an attacker permanently own the displayed author of any line they touch by one character — e.g. insert a space into a victim's line, or attribute their own defamatory text to the victim. The gutter presents this as fact ("who last edited each line", editor.ts:122) with no trust indicator; homoglyph/RTL-override or zero-width names sharpen the impersonation (`author.trim() === ''` only catches pure whitespace, blame-gutter.ts:51). Mitigating: docs/design/notes/notes.md explicitly calls blame "a reading aid, not an audit trail" — but that caveat is not surfaced in the UI. Amplifier, pre-existing and out of diff: the auth webhook runs in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true'` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:86-105), so today even the editor-role gate is not enforced.

samples.summary: Authorship is recorded unconditionally, even for users who never enable the opt-in feature — no consent or opt-out for having your name written into the document
samples.evidence: The feature is documented as strictly opt-in: "a reader who never turns it on gets a note identical to before — same layout, same line width, and none of the per-edit bookkeeping" (docs/design/notes/notes.md, blame-gutter subsection) and "Nothing changes for someone who never turns it on" (docs/tasks/active/20260822-notes-blame-gutter-todo.md). Only the *read* path is gated (`showAuthors` compartments, editor.ts:356/388). The *write* at yorkie-note-store.ts:90-94 is unconditional: every user's username and edit timestamps are recorded into the shared, replicated document whether or not they (or anyone) enabled the gutter, with no setting to suppress it and no notice. Combined with the exposure vector above, a user cannot avoid publishing their edit metadata to everyone who can read the note. Not exploitable on its own; a privacy-by-default gap and a code/doc mismatch on a privacy claim.

samples.summary: Quadratic label recomputation over an attacker-inflatable run count can freeze a viewer's editor (client-side resource exhaustion)
samples.evidence: `computeBlameLabels` calls `authorOfRange` per line (blame-gutter.ts:65-74), and `authorOfRange` rescans the span array from index 0 for every line, only breaking once `span.from >= to` (blame-gutter.ts:43-49) — so cost is O(lines x spans) and the whole walk (`store.getAuthorSpans()`, which iterates every CRDT run) runs on every `docChanged` update, i.e. per keystroke, while the gutter is on. Run count is now driven by edit count rather than note length (each insert creates an attributed run), and a co-editor or anonymous editor-role share-link visitor can deliberately spray many single-character edits to inflate runs into the 10^5 range. Any user who then enables "Show authors" on that note pays lines x spans work per keystroke, which can hang the tab. I did not measure the actual threshold, hence low confidence on exploitability; the algorithmic shape is directly visible in the cited lines.

verdict.reason: The described code exists exactly as claimed: editText stamps CRDT attributes {a: username, t: Date.now()} on every non-empty insert (yorkie-note-store.ts:84-99), share-link visitors attach to the same note document with their username in presence (shared-document.tsx:883-897, :838/:890), and the Yorkie auth webhook grants read to any share-link holder regardless of role (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:196-200). However this is not blocking under the security rubric: there is no authorization bypass (the reader holds a valid link that already authorizes reading the note's full contents over that same channel) and no secret/credential/token exposure — only a username string and an epoch-ms timestamp. Moreover the identical class of data is already persisted at rest in the same Yorkie replication channel for the pre-existing share-visible document types: CommentAuthor{userId, username, photo} plus createdAt/editedAt epoch-ms timestamps (packages/sheets/src/comment/types.ts:1-36) are stored directly in the docs and pdf Yorkie roots (docs-document.ts:24, pdf-document.ts:11), readable by viewer-role share visitors through the very same webhook allowance. Note presence itself already ships username/email/photo to any attached share visitor (notes-document.ts:25-32, shared-document.tsx:887-893), so username visibility to viewer links is an accepted product property, and the new attribution carries strictly less identifying data than what already replicates. What remains is a privacy/product-scoping question (should authorship metadata be gated separately from document read access?) — a hardening/minor item, not a major security weakness or an exploitable auth/secret/injection/crypto defect.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: the blame author string comes solely from client-set presence (yorkie-note-store.ts:134-142) and is written as client-controlled Text attributes `a`/`t` (yorkie-note-store.ts:90-97), with presence `name` assigned by the client at attach (notes-detail.tsx:259, shared-document.tsx:890, defaulting to "Anonymous" for share-link visitors). The gutter renders the largest-`at` run's name verbatim as authoritative (blame-gutter.ts:37-52, 103-111). I searched the entire backend for any verification: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:116-204 authorizes only doc key + verb (and grants `rw` to anonymous `link.role === 'editor'` at line 200, with shadow-mode bypass at lines 86-105); yorkie-event.controller.ts:37-62 handles only `updatedAt`; yorkie-admin.service.ts:278-286 consumes presence usernames without validating them; no sanitizer/validator for presence or Text attributes exists anywhere. So the absence claim holds — no counterexample found. Impact is identity spoofing: any writer, including an unauthenticated share-link editor, can attribute arbitrary text to a named victim and pin it with a far-future `t`. The only mitigation is a design-doc caveat (docs/design/notes/notes.md:540-543), not surfaced in the UI. This is an authenticity/impersonation weakness within the security lane, matching the reviewer's `major` severity.
